questions.question: Find LCM of 9/4, 21/10, 63/20.
questions.solution:
**Given: **

To find LCM of 9/4, 21/10, 63/20.

**Concept:** LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators/HCF of Denominators

**Calculation: **

The given fractions are

⇒ 9/4,21/10,63/20

Numerators of the given fractions are

⇒ 9,21,63

⇒ LCM (9,21,63) = 63

Denominators of the given fractions are

⇒ 4,10,20

⇒ HCF (4,10,20) = 2

Using the concept

LCM of given fractions = LCM (9,21,63) / HCF (4,10,20)

LCM of given fractions = 63/2

∴** The correct answer is 63/2.**

questions.question: M1 alone can do a work in 14 days and M2 alone can do the same work in 70 days. With help of M3, they finish the same work in 7 days. In how many days M3 alone can do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

M1 takes 14 days, M2 takes 70 days and M1, M2 and M3 together take 7 days to complete a work.

**Concept:** 

If 'A', 'B' and 'C' work together, then their combined work done in one day will be = 1/X + 1/Y + 1/Z.

**Calculation:**

Let M3 alone takes p number of days to complete a work.

One day work of M1, M2 and M3 will be,

⇒ M1= 1/14

⇒ M2 = 1/70

⇒ M3 = 1/p

Together they complete work in 7 days, 

⇒ M1+M2+M3 = 1/7 

 Using the concept,

⇒ 1/7 = 1/14 + 1/70 + 1/p 

⇒ 1/7 = (5+1)/70 + 1/p

⇒ 1/p = 1/7 - 6/70

⇒ 1/p = (10- 6)/70

 ⇒ 1/p = 4/70

⇒ p = 70/4

⇒ p = 35/2 

So, M3 alone can do the same work in 17.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__ If a person 'A' takes X days to complete a work, then in one day work done will be = 1/X.

 If a person 'B' takes Y days to complete a work, then in one day work done will be = 1/Y.

 If a person 'C' takes Z days to complete a work, then in one day work done will be = 1/Z.

questions.question: If a number R1 is 13 percent less than another number R2 and R2 is 50 percent more than 5600 , then what is the value of R1?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

R1 is 13% less than R2 and R2 is 50% more than 5600.

**Concept:** If any number 'A' is X% less/more than any number 'B', then A is,

For less, A = B × (100 - X)/100

For more, A = B × (100 + X)/100 

**Calculation: **

R2 is 50% more than 5600.

⇒ R2 = 5600 × (100 + 50)/100 

⇒ R2 = 5600 × 150/100 

⇒ R2 = 56 × 150 

⇒ R2 = 8400

Now, R1 is 13% less than R2.

⇒ R1 = 8400 × (100 - 13)/100 

⇒ R1 = 8400 × 87/100 

⇒ R1 = 84 × 87

⇒ R1 = 7308

**∴ The correct answer is 7308.**

Mohan buys an old mobile for Rs. 4000 and spends Rs. 500 on its repairs. If he sells the mobile for Rs. 5000, then what is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Cost price of mobile = Rs. 4000, Repair cost = Rs. 500 and Selling Price = Rs. 5000.

**Formula used:**

Profit Percentage = [(Selling price - Actual Cost price)/ Actual Cost price] × 100 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

Actual Cost price is the total of buying cost, repair cost, and transportation cost etc.

**Calculation:**

Actual Cost price = Cost price of mobile + Repair cost

⇒ 4000 + 500

⇒ Rs. 4500 

Now, profit percentage,

⇒ [(5000 - 4500)/4500] × 100 

⇒ [500/4500] × 100

⇒ 100/9

⇒ 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 25 percent more than its cost price. What is the maximum discount percentage at which the shopkeeper sells his article with no profit or no loss?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : MP = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5.

For no profit/loss, SP must be equal to CP, so SP = 4 units.

Discount allowed = MP − SP = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 25%

Condition = No profit or loss (SP = CP)

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31c759cfa518c1f3afcfa8836f55064a51b00845abf53d14b1ab802049e9db75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) of the article = ₹100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 25% of CP = 100 + 25 = ₹125

⇒ Since there is no profit and no loss, Selling Price (SP) = CP = ₹100

⇒ Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

⇒ Discount = 125 − 100 = ₹25

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (25 ÷ 125) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the CP is increased to get the MP. MP = CP × [1 + (Markup% ÷ 100)].

Relationship between Markup, Discount and Profit

Net Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − [(Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100]. If Profit = 0, then Markup% − Discount% = (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)].

questions.question: After deducting 10 percent from a certain sum and then deducting 70 percent from the remainder, 1188 is left. What was that sum?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Deduction 10% and 70% from the remainder and then 1188 is left from the sum.

**Concept used:** If X% is deducted from any number 'N', then the remaining number is = N × (100 - X) /100. 

**Calculation:**

Let the number be N.

After the 10% deduction, the number becomes, 

⇒ N × (100-10)/100

⇒ 9N/10.

Now, deducting 70% from the remainder, the number becomes,

⇒ 9N/10 × (100-70)/100

⇒ 9N/10 × 3/10

⇒ 27N/100 

which is equal to 1188.

The value of N is,

27N/100 = 1188

N= 44 × 100

N =4400

**∴ The correct answer is 4400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__ **Successive deductions/discounts of a% and b% is equivalent to a + b -(a × b)/100. Total deduction = 10 + 70 - (10 × 70)/100

⇒ 80-7

⇒ 73% 

So, remaining part is 27%.

(27/100) × N = 1188 

N = 4400.

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 15 cm is melted and recast into a cone having diameter of the base as 15 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of sphere = 15cm and diameter of base of cone = 15cm to find height 'h' of cone.

**Concept used: **

When a solid body recast into other body volume remain same.

Formulas used: 

Volume of sphere = 4/3π r³

Volume of cone = 1/3π r²h.

**Calculation:**

Using the concept equating volume of both the solids equal.

 ⇒ 4/3π (15)³ = 1/3π (15/2)2 h.

⇒4 × 15 = 1/4× h

⇒h = 240cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 240cm.**

questions.question: A person borrowed Rs. 15000 on compound interest at the rate of 30 percent per annum. If the interest is compounded half yearly, then what will be the amount to be paid after 1 year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 15000, Rate = 30% compounded half yearly to find the amount to be paid after 1 year.

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal (1 + rate/100)time

Concept used: 

If the rate is compounded half yearly, then the effective rate be half and time period be twice. Effective rate = 30/2 = 15% and time period = 2. 

**Calculation:**

Amount at the end of 1 year,

⇒ 15000 (1 + 15/100 )²

⇒ 15000 × 23/20 × 23/20 

⇒ Rs. 19837.5 

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 19837.5.**

questions.question: Three rectangular fields having areas of 70 m², 84 m², and 112 m2 are to be divided into identical rectangular flower beds, each having a length of 7 m. Find the breadth of each flower bed.
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Three rectangular fields having areas of 70 m2, 84 m2, and 112 m², needed to divide into identical rectangular flower beds of length 7m to find breadth of each flower bed.

**Formula used:**

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

**Concept used:**

Area of identical flower beds mean the HCF of areas of three rectangular fields that is HCF (70, 84, 112) = 14m².

**Calculation:**

Area = 7 × breadth 

14 = 7 × breadth 

breadth = 2m.

**∴ The correct answer is 2m**.
